In "The Need to Speak Caste," first-generation Dalit scholar Suraj Yungde confronts deep-seated caste beliefs with profound insights and personal experiences. Growing up in a Dalit community, Yungde shares moving anecdotes from his life, illustrating the pain and struggles of daily existence and how love and faith helped him overcome these challenges. He sheds light on the invisible barriers within politics, bureaucracy, and the justice system, revealing systemic inequalities. Addressing internal caste divisions, the behavior of upper-caste Dalits, and the persistence of untouchability in the modern world, Yungde courageously and honestly exposes the pervasive impact of Brahminical ideologies. This book is a compelling exploration of caste dynamics and the quest for social justice.
